# GB Electricity

> A live dashboard for the Great Britain electricity system: generation mix, national and
> underlying demand, wind and solar, interconnector flows, carbon intensity and grid
> frequency. Figures come from Elexon Insights (BMRS), the NESO Carbon Intensity API and
> Sheffield Solar PV_Live, and are refreshed continuously. The project's aim is the
> clearest explanation of Britain's electricity system, so every figure states its
> source, its boundary and its age.

## Pages

- [Live dashboard](https://gbelectricity.uk/): The whole system on one page — what is generating now, what
  the country is drawing, and what is changing.
- [Methodology](https://gbelectricity.uk/methodology): What each figure on the live dashboard means, how it is derived from the public feeds, and where the data can mislead you.
- [About GB Electricity](https://gbelectricity.uk/about): The provenance of the data, every endpoint the page calls, the licences that come with them, and where the project stands.
- [Generation](https://gbelectricity.uk/generation): The GB mix changes every five minutes as fuels are dispatched against demand and price. This page follows it over 24 hours and seven days, and sets each fuel’s share of the electricity against its share of the carbon.
- [Demand](https://gbelectricity.uk/demand): GB demand follows a daily shape set by weather, work and daylight. This page tracks today’s curve against the forecast ahead — and why three published figures for GB demand can all be right at once.
- [Interconnectors](https://gbelectricity.uk/interconnectors): Ten subsea and tunnel cables connect Great Britain to six countries. This page tracks what each one is doing right now.
- [Carbon intensity](https://gbelectricity.uk/carbon-intensity): GB’s carbon intensity turns the live fuel mix into a single number — grams of CO₂ per kWh — judged against bands that shift every year as the grid cleans up. This page tracks that figure over 24 hours against its forecast, and sets each fuel’s share of generation against its share of the emissions.
- [System](https://gbelectricity.uk/system): GB’s grid has to keep generation and demand matched to the megawatt, every second — frequency is the physical sign of how well that’s going. This page tracks it three ways, on three timescales — a real-time reading, a forecast imbalance and a settled outcome — and why they can point in different directions without anything being wrong.
- [Batteries](https://gbelectricity.uk/batteries): Great Britain’s grid-scale batteries buy and sell power in minutes, smoothing the gaps between generation and demand. This page tracks the fleet’s real net position — charging or discharging — and how much of that is the fleet trading on its own account versus NESO instructing it directly.

## Using this data

- The figures are derived, not republished: see the methodology page for how each one is
  calculated and what the public feeds cannot see.
- Elexon's BMRS data is used under its Licence to use BMRS open data, which prescribes its
  attribution verbatim; NESO's Carbon Intensity data is CC BY 4.0. The about page carries
  every endpoint, licence and attribution in full.
- The dashboard renders its figures in the browser from live API calls, so a fetch of the
  HTML alone will not contain current values.
